$comment: Execution-loop bookkeeping for automated contributors. Not consumed by the
crate at build or run time; nothing in src/ or tests/ reads this file.
Kept in-tree so a later cycle (or a different session) can see what has
already been tried and, more importantly, what was tried and REJECTED —
the rejected list is the part that stops cycles rediscovering the same
verified_against: cargo test --all --locked (5953 lib + 117 api + 56 smoke + all integration suites, 0 failed), cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings (clean), cargo fmt --all -- --check (clean), node --check on every modified JS module. NOT verified on this host: the MSRV 1.88 pin and the aarch64-linux-android cross-build (no Android NDK present) — CI's aarch64-android job is the authority.

cycle_1_slots.instruction: Decide and record the DbWriter unbounded-channel question (OD-1).
cycle_1_slots.status: COMPLETE — DECIDED: keep the channel unbounded, and disclose a pathological backlog. Bounding it would force try_send (drops events, breaking the flush() contract) or an async submit() at a sync engine call site. The queue is also already bounded in practice by DEFAULT_MAX_ENTITIES=2500 and the wall-time watchdog. The real defect was that a storage stall was INVISIBLE, so writer_loop now discloses queue depth past BACKLOG_WARN_EVENTS=1024 with hysteresis at half.

cycle_2_slots.instruction: Make app::update::self_restart honour its documented contract on current_exe() failure.
cycle_2_slots.status: COMPLETE (2597c1f9) — the fn documents 'prints a diagnostic and exits with code 1' but current_exe().expect(...) panicked. current_exe() is a real syscall (/proc/self/exe) and this is the site most likely to see it fail: a self-restart runs right after an update rewrote or unlinked the running binary.

A 47-event scan logged `⚡ High cross-source corroboration` nine times byte-identically (12 correlations total). cycle_3_slots.instruction: Remove the per-event O(n) work the scan views do in the browser during a live scan.
cycle_3_slots.status: COMPLETE (d72041e1) — two hot paths, both behaviour-preserving. (a) scan_info/graph.js resolved correlation-hub corroboration with S.entities.find(...) nested two loops deep: O(correlations x members x entities); a captured 371-entity / 32-correlation scan is millions of string compares per re-layout. Now a uid->entity Map, the pattern the file already used for nodesById. (b) scan_info/log.js re-sorted the type histogram, rewrote its innerHTML, and read box.scrollHeight (forcing synchronous layout) once PER EVENT — ~600 full re-renders and ~600 forced reflows for a 598-event scan. Both are idempotent and only the last is observable, so they coalesce into one animation frame; counting stays synchronous so the breakdown still covers every event.

cycle_3_slots.instruction: Drop the vendored D3 force layout; make the graph extremely basic without losing functionality.
cycle_3_slots.status: COMPLETE (77e73134) — D3 v3 was the last vendored front-end asset (151,725 B) and its continuous force simulation was the most expensive thing the UI did, running over hundreds of nodes on the same device running the scan. Replaced by a deterministic concentric SVG layout computed once in O(nodes), drawn against the DOM with pointer events. Preserved: kind colours, corroboration radius, truncated labels, tooltips, legend, #graph-cap notice, GEXF, Re-layout, Reset view, node drag, canvas pan, pinch/scroll zoom, and every ceiling (GRAPH_MAX_NODES/LINKS, CORR_MAX_SPOKES, star-not-clique). src/web 583,772 -> 439,346 B (-24.7%) and the same bytes leave the binary; VENDOR_FILES is now empty. Deleted a bug class too: the old D3-v3 string-endpoint guard test is obsolete, replaced by one asserting the engine cannot creep back and no per-frame loop runs.

observations.summary: OB-4 RESOLVED, and my earlier smtp_vrfy hypothesis was WRONG. Device debug bundles show `status : Running` — the operator exported them mid-scan, so a log ending at a bare `module >` line is an export boundary, not a hang. Confirmed by counter-example: the 535-event log cuts at `> emailrep` while `smtp_vrfy` COMPLETED in that same run (`smtp_vrfy (1 found)`), and the 598-event log cuts at `> smtp_vrfy`. Different terminal modules, no fixed event cap (598 vs 535) — consistent with export-while-running, not with any one module hanging.
observations.action: closed — do not re-open on log truncation alone

observations.summary: OPEN BUG, not yet fixed: the debug bundle's FULL DOSSIER header prints `modules : 0 run, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 skipped, 0 cached, 0 deduped` while the SAME scan's event log records 60 module_done, 9 module_error, 11 module_skipped, 70 module_start (entities 264, status Running). The module counters are dead zeros in the dossier. Cause not yet established — likely the counters are only populated at scan completion, or the dossier reads a default/fresh stats struct. Needs the renderer located (grep for "timed out" / "deduped") and the data source traced before a fix.

(a) Production `.unwrap()` count is genuinely 0; the 55 production `.expect()` hits are infallible-by-construction (literal Regex::new, aho-corasick over static patterns, tokio runtime / reqwest client init) — the earlier rejection of 'eliminate unwrap/panic/unsafe' is correct as written. (d) modules/dns_axfr is safe AND already proptested (extract_name_is_total, extract_name_rejects_pointer_loops, build_axfr_query_is_total) — a totality proptest there would be pure duplication.

observations.summary: UNRESOLVED, needs device-side evidence: the 598-event log ends at `04:55:25 module ▶ smtp_vrfy` with no matching ✓/✗ and NO `scan complete` line, whereas the 47-event log terminates cleanly with `✔ scan complete · 10 entities`. Either the scan hung/died in smtp_vrfy (plausible — it dials port 25, which mobile carriers routinely blackhole, so a connect can stall past any read timeout) or the export simply truncated at 598 events. Cannot distinguish from the log alone.
observations.action: open — before treating as a defect, confirm whether the exporter caps event count; if it does not, audit smtp_vrfy's connect timeout specifically (a read timeout does not bound a TCP connect that never completes)

observations.summary: `cargo tree --duplicates` reports getrandom at v0.2.17, v0.3.4 and v0.4.3. All three are transitive and not directly reachable from this crate's manifest: 0.2 via ring -> rustls -> reqwest, 0.3 via proptest -> rand_core (a dev-dependency only), 0.4 separately. Deduplicating would mean forcing versions on ring/rustls, which is a larger risk than the duplication.
observations.action: none — recorded so a later cycle does not re-derive it

observations.observation: CLOSES OB-6. The mid-scan six-zero module counters are fully explained and fixed in cycle 4 slot 1. Evidence chain: Scan::new seeds zeros (core/scan/mod.rs) -> run_with_ledger_inner upserts Running with them (core/engine/mod.rs:653-654) -> finalise_scan is the sole writer (core/engine/mod.rs:991-996). Both uploaded debug bundles were status:Running, which is why both showed zeros while their event streams held ~70 module_start / ~60 module_done / ~9 module_error / ~11 module_skipped.

Deliberate design limit recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the event stream CANNOT reconstruct the engine's six counters. There is no distinct EventKind for a timeout (it arrives as a plain ModuleError), a cache replay, or a dedup; and ModuleSkipped is not disjoint from ModuleStart — gate-skips are emitted with no preceding start (Engine::emit_module_skipped, core/engine/mod.rs:477-482) while dispatched-then-opted-out modules emit one first (dispatch.rs:548). ModuleEventTally therefore reports event counts under their event names and offers no in-flight figure.
observations.action: documented on the type; no further work

observations.observation: VERIFIED NEGATIVES for the Termux web-UI crash sweep, so future cycles do not re-investigate. (a) No leaked listeners or observers: every document/window listener (ui.js initMoreSheet/initModals/initTableLabels, helpers.js initDownloads, theme.js, main.js hashchange) is attached exactly once at bootstrap in main.js:113-116, and initDownloads is additionally idempotent via window.__hseDownloadsInit. (b) graph.js attaches only to the svg and to node elements, all inside the replaced subtree, so they are collected with the DOM. (c) Auto-refresh timers cannot stack: main.js render() calls clearScanTimer/clearLiveTimer/clearEnginesTimer/clearOptsTimers before dispatching, and scan-info arms its timer only after its render completes. (d) browse.js was already capped (BROWSE_ROW_CAP) and graph.js already capped (GRAPH_MAX_NODES/GRAPH_MAX_LINKS/CORR_MAX_SPOKES); log.js was the only uncapped per-event view, fixed in slot 2.

STILL OPEN, not addressed this cycle. scan_info/index.js fetches ALL FOUR of scan, entities, correlations and relations on every render regardless of which tab is active (index.js:24-26), including the 8s live refresh. The full entity set carries complete evidence chains, so on a large scan this is the heaviest single thing the UI does. Slot 3 stopped it happening for a hidden tab, which removes the unattended case, but a visible scan-info tab still re-pulls everything every 8s. A per-tab fetch projection (or a lightweight counts endpoint for the header stat cards, given scan.entity_count is already in the scan record) would cut it further.
observations.action: open — candidate for a future cycle; needs a browser to validate, which this host does not have

open_defects.summary: DbWriter uses mpsc::unbounded_channel (src/core/engine/writer.rs:39). If event production outpaces sqlite batch writes the queue grows without bound, on a platform whose whole point is a memory-constrained no-root Android device. Exposure INCREASED when #315 raised DEFAULT_SCAN_DEPTH 3->5, since more rounds means more events.

cycle_4_slots.instruction: Establish why the dossier/debug bundle prints six zero module counters mid-scan, then fix it without fabricating numbers.
cycle_4_slots.outcome: DONE (d4238fa9b). Cause traced end to end: Scan::new seeds modules_* to 0; run_with_ledger_inner (core/engine/mod.rs:653) upserts the Running row with those zeros; the ONLY write is finalise_scan (core/engine/mod.rs:991-996) at scan end; nothing updates the row in between. Fix is disclosure + the number that does exist: ScanStatus::is_terminal(), a NOT-YET-FINAL caveat appended by module_accounting_line() on non-terminal scans (inherited by both renderers from the one single-sourced sentence), and core::event::ModuleEventTally rendered by render_full as an 'observed :' line on the non-terminal path only. 7 tests.

cycle_4_slots.instruction: Bound the web scan-log DOM so a long scan cannot exhaust a Termux browser tab, without silently truncating what the operator can save.
cycle_4_slots.outcome: DONE (e5899aac9). appendLog created one permanent node per event and removed nothing. LOG_MAX_ROWS=1200, oldest-first, evicted synchronously inside appendLog (a deferred trim would still let the full list exist for a frame during the synchronous history render; the peak is the problem). Disclosed three ways: the By-type breakdown counts events not rows so its totals stay complete, it names the drop and points at Download, and the 'Save shown' header warns the file starts mid-scan.

cycle_4_slots.instruction: Stop the three timer-driven views doing full network + render work while nobody is looking at them.
cycle_4_slots.outcome: DONE (5f6475bb3). scan-info (8s, four requests + full view rebuild), Live monitor (8s), Engines (30s server-side liveness sweep) all now consult a shared timers.js pageHidden(). Schedule is kept rather than torn down: a hidden tick fires, does nothing, re-arms — chosen over a visibilitychange listener specifically because scan-info re-renders every 8s and would accumulate one listener per render.

cycle_4_slots.instruction: Make the Graph tab usable during a running scan — the 8s refresh was discarding the operator's viewport.
cycle_4_slots.outcome: DONE (45fcd1f61). `const view` was declared inside buildGraph, so every 8s rebuild snapped the canvas to origin at scale 1 and the graph could not be panned or zoomed for the whole duration of a scan. Hoisted to module scope, re-applied by buildGraph's closing applyView(), reset per-scan via viewScanId so a different scan starts centred. Node positions deliberately not preserved (layoutConcentric is deterministic; a growing node set legitimately relayouts) and the comment says so.
